result:
The proposed answer of 21 is wrong. The minimum is 1, but the second-smallest value is at least 22.

**Reformulation.** Write $f(x)=4(x-p)$, $g(x)=6(x-q)$, $h(x)=9(x-s)$ with $p=-a/4$, $q=-b/6$, $s=-c/9$. The inverse maps are $T_f(y)=y/4+p$, $T_g(y)=y/6+q$, $T_h(y)=y/9+s$. The root of a word is obtained by applying the inverse maps in turn to $0$. So if $V_n$ is the set of roots of length-$n$ compositions, then $V_0=\{0\}$ and $V_n=\bigcup_{w\in\{f,g,h\}} T_w(V_{n-1})$, and $R=|V_{20}|$.

**The claimed $R=1$ argument is false.** If $p=q=s$, the roots are not all equal. For example, $f(g(x))=24x-28$ has root $7/6$ when $p=q=s=1$, while $f(f(x))$ has root $5/4$. $R=1$ occurs only for $p=q=s=0$ (i.e., $a=b=c=0$).

**Growth is at least $n+1$, but not tightly.** Let $m=|V_{n-1}|$. Each $T_w(V_{n-1})$ has $m$ points, so $|V_n|\ge m$. If $|V_n|=m\ge 2$, all three images coincide, so $\sigma=T_g^{-1}T_f$ permutes $V_{n-1}$. Then some power of $\sigma$ (ratio $(3/2)^k\ne1$) fixes $m\ge2$ points, which is impossible. So $|V_n|\ge|V_{n-1}|+1$ whenever $|V_{n-1}|\ge2$. Also $|V_2|\ge3$ when $R>1$. This gives $R\ge 21$, but the proposed solution never proves attainability.

**Exactly 21 is impossible.** The proposed example $a=4t,\ b=6t,\ c=9t$ gives $p=q=s=-t$. With $p=q=s=1$, $V_2=\{5/4,7/6,10/9\}$ and $V_3$ has 9 distinct points, so this example does not give 21.

More generally, suppose $|V_{n-1}|=3$ and $|V_n|=4$. Let $X=V_{n-1}$ and let $P_{fg},P_{fh},P_{gh}$ be the numbers of path components of the restricted maps $\sigma_{fg}=T_g^{-1}T_f$ (ratio $3/2$), $\sigma_{fh}$ (ratio $9/4$), and $\sigma_{gh}$ (ratio $3/2$) on $X$. Inclusion–exclusion gives $|V_n|=\sum P+t$, where $t=|T_f(X)\cap T_g(X)\cap T_h(X)|$. A full chain under a ratio-$\lambda$ map has sorted gap ratio $\lambda$ or $1/\lambda$, so a full $3/2$-chain and a full $9/4$-chain cannot coexist. Checking the cases $\sum P+t=4$ shows each one is contradictory. Hence no step from 3 to 4 is possible.

Combining these: if $R>1$ then $|V_2|\ge3$, and the step from size 3 cannot increase by exactly 1. So $R\ge 22$ whenever $R>1$, and 21 cannot occur.

VERDICT: REJECT
